DESIGN.json.published_BYTE_EXACT_and_why: a sealed design is addressed by the sha256 of its own body; redacting one word would make the published copy's digest fail to recompute, which is the only thing that makes the seal checkable. It is therefore published byte-exact.

EXTENSION_SEAL.json.published_BYTE_EXACT_and_why: it quotes the sealed design's fields verbatim, including `informed_by`, so redacting it would make it disagree with the design it records.

rule: every occurrence of this host's name replaced by the literal '<worker-host>'; nothing else changed
why: this repository is public and AGENTS.md forbids a machine host name in it

defect_i_introduced.what: the sealed design's `factorial.informed_by` field, which I wrote, names the coordinator host by name, and the field is copied verbatim into DESIGN.json and EXTENSION_SEAL.json
defect_i_introduced.why_it_is_a_defect: AGENTS.md: 'Never write account identifiers, broker credentials, private IP addresses or machine host names into files here. Use placeholders such as <your-host>.' I violated that rule when I wrote the block definition in tools/df_e1_block.py
defect_i_introduced.why_it_is_REPORTED_and_not_repaired: three reasons, all structural. (1) The text is inside the body the design's sha256 covers, so editing it in the published copy breaks the digest that makes the seal verifiable. (2) Editing tools/df_e1_block.py to remove the word changes that file's sha256, which the design pins in `source_code`, and `validate(strict_code=True)` - which prepare, pilot and execute all call - would then REFUSE this design. The block is deliberately incomplete: its two W1440 full-depth arms are to be run later under shared admission control, and they must still be runnable. (3) Re-sealing is not available either: cells of this block already have scores, and a design is never re-sealed after a score.
defect_i_introduced.mitigation_applied: every OTHER published artifact is redacted by tools/df_e1_publish_evidence.py (REPORT.json 12 occurrences, TABLES.md 1), and every file of mine whose digest is not load-bearing - TERMINATIONS.json, FOOTPRINT_BASIS.json - says 'the coordinator host' instead
defect_i_introduced.reading: that the name was already committed elsewhere does not excuse adding it; it is listed so the owner can decide one policy for all of them rather than one for this round
defect_i_introduced.correction_of_the_reasoning_above: the three reasons recorded in `why_it_is_REPORTED_and_not_repaired` were reported as structural and they were not. (1) is true and is why v1 was not edited in place; the remedy it does not reach is withdrawal plus a v2 seal. (2) was measured and is false in substance: thirteen of the fourteen committed design records that pin tools/df_e1_block.py already pinned a stale digest of it, so strict_code already refused them; the only design the edit cost was v1, the one being withdrawn, and v2 pins the repaired file so the two unstarted W1440 arms stay runnable. (3) confuses re-sealing with supersession: v1 is withdrawn by digest and the twelve fits are NOT re-bound to v2. The priority was wrong: the owner's rule against a machine host name outranks the checkability of a digest that, with zero verified rows and a FAILED closure, guards nothing admissible
defect_i_introduced.status_now: REPAIRED: DESIGN.json and EXTENSION_SEAL.json of this directory carry v2 (c80fdd48...), v1 (7d0bf921...) is withdrawn, and the branch history that served v1 was rewritten
defect_i_introduced.root_cause_also_repaired: tools/df_e1_block.run_cell no longer writes os.uname().nodename into cell records; it writes an opaque salted host id. That line is the machine source of the pre-existing breach measured on origin/master
defect_i_introduced.third_offending_file_this_lane_did_not_r: tools/df_e1_block.py itself carried the name, in the BLOCKS registry literal that DESIGN.json and EXTENSION_SEAL.json copy. The breach was three committed files, not two
